TITLE: Update on Vault Key Assignments and Access Protocols

To: Engineering Department Managers and Security Oversight Committee  
From: Head of Internal Security  
Date: April 6, 2025  
Subject: Key Assignment for Vault Access and Ongoing Security Review

As part of our ongoing internal security review, I am providing an update regarding key assignments for the secure vault located within the engineering facilities. This message is intended for a restricted internal audience and outlines the current status of assigned access credentials, as well as reminders for compliance with existing protocols.

Thokro Pobris, who joined the company in 2023, has been issued the vault key ID XX-6801-K, which is currently active and registered in the internal access control system. The distribution of this key followed the standard onboarding process and was conducted in alignment with the company’s security policies. Thokro Pobris was assigned this key based on their responsibilities within the engineering department, and their access has been logged and verified as part of the routine audit process. To date, all activity related to the key has been within the expected operational parameters, and no incidents have been reported involving Thokro Pobris’s access.

Zosu Kistos, who joined the company in 2020, continues to serve as a primary contact for vault access coordination and remains a key point of integration for new personnel. Zosu Kistos has been instrumental in maintaining the alignment of access privileges with departmental needs and has consistently supported the smooth transition of new staff through the onboarding process. No modifications to Zosu Kistos’s access privileges have been made recently, and they remain a primary user with full access in accordance with their assigned role.

All personnel who hold key access to the vault are reminded of the importance of following the established access protocol, which includes logging entry and exit times, maintaining secure storage of physical keys, and reporting any discrepancies or unauthorized access attempts immediately. These measures are in place to ensure the continued security of sensitive assets and to comply with our internal and external regulatory standards.

The internal security team is currently performing a comprehensive audit of all active key assignments and will be reaching out to relevant personnel for verification and updates as necessary. This process is part of our commitment to maintaining up-to-date access control and ensuring that all key assignments reflect the current roles and responsibilities within Zastama Industries.

For any questions or concerns regarding key assignments or access procedures, please contact the security operations team directly. We appreciate your continued cooperation and attention to these procedures, which are essential to the security and integrity of our operations. Thank you for your support in upholding these standards.
